heard: Early spacewalking was so exhausting it nearly killed astronauts. Pilots couldn't work in zero gravity without proper body restraints. NASA launched Gemini 12 in November 1966 to fix this crisis. Command pilot James Lovell and pilot Buzz Aldrin faced radar failure. Aldrin used a sextant to manually compute their orbital rendezvous maneuvers. He then tested custom foot restraints during three difficult spacewalks. Underwater pool training had finally mastered the deadly zero gravity fatigue. Spacewalk exhaustion nearly killed astronauts before underwater pools saved missions.
